title: Normalized big-fppf ringed comparison and tensor-section extension for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $W$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. A small presentation $B$ of the big fppf site is a small category in the ambient universe with a fully faithful essentially surjective functor to the category of the algebraic spaces over $W$ in the fixed bound. Its covering families are exactly the fppf families [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. It includes the scheme objects of the small etale site, compatibly with the enlarged etale model [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Define the normalized big ringed comparison data as follows. The ring sheaf has at $v:V\to W$ the ring $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ of compatible regular functions on all small-etale scheme charts; its operations are chartwise, and its restrictions pull regular functions back along each commuting pair of charts. Restriction to the small etale site is the structure sheaf, with the canonical common ambient-universe lift of its carriers; the restriction isomorphism on each chart is normalized using the specified isomorphism between the two inclusions of that etale object. Inclusion is continuous, and its sheaf restriction is the direct image of a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. The structural-ring isomorphism defines module direct image as actual restriction of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a small-etale module $M$, a normalized section extension $M^a$ is a module sheaf on $B$ with specified additive and scalar-compatible bijections $M^a(V)\simeq\Gamma(V,v^*M)$; here $v^*$ and its local tensors are the canonical module operations [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For every arrow $h:V'\to V$, these bijections identify restriction with tensor pullback of sections followed by the canonical tensor-composition isomorphism [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]. The direct-image functor is additive, and its source has enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], so its right derived functors are computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. This defines the normalized data and section-extension predicate; it does not choose an arbitrary functor, ring map or extension. All section formulas quantify over every chart, without a finiteness or separation condition.
